launcher_icon._doc: The launcher icon, generated from this declaration by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-launcher-icons.py (pattern + category colours + glyphs in 1_cicd/src/data/launcher-icons.json). Never edit the generated res files.

name: cloud-media-center
description: The fleet's media hub, as an APK, in Rust and static web only: a Tauri 2 app whose one webview shows seven mobile-first pages — music, videos, gallery, books, feed, movies, documentaries — built from the media data of diegonmarcos.github.io pinned at one commit. Every link out goes to the phone's own apps through tauri-plugin-opener.
_doc: WHY TAURI. Same shape as ac_cloud-c3-webserver (the fleet's first Tauri app): src-tauri/ is a Rust library that starts the Tauri runtime with tauri-plugin-opener, and its one window shows web/, which tauri.conf.json::build.frontendDist bundles into the APK. There is no server and no network fetch at runtime: the pages read web/data/*.json, generated by data/regen.py from diegonmarcos.github.io at data.source.commit. The only Kotlin in the tree is the glue Tauri's Android template generates (tauri.glue, every file pinned by sha256); test/test-media-center-no-kotlin.sh fails the CI run and build.sh fails the build on anything else. NAME: cloud-media-center was the gallery app's name until 2026-10; that app is now cloud-gallery (ac_cloud-gallery, com.diegonmarcos.mediacenter) and this one has its own applicationId.

tauri._doc: THE ONE declaration of how the APK is built. crate_dir is the Tauri app crate (its [lib] is lib_name, the .so Tauri's generated activity loads); web_dir is the static frontend tauri.conf.json bundles; android_project is the Tauri-generated gradle project, committed as Tauri recommends; targets maps each Android ABI a release variant names to the key `cargo tauri android build --target` takes (tauri) and the Rust triple the workflow installs for it (rust). Always Tauri's release profile (R8 + an optimised, stripped Rust library), and build.sh re-signs every APK with the shared key.

glue._doc: The ONLY Kotlin/Java files the app may commit: Tauri 2.12.1's Android template (templates/mobile/android in the tauri-cli crate) rendered for this identifier, byte for byte. A file here whose bytes change, a .kt/.java/standalone .kts anywhere else in the app, or a file listed here that is missing fails test/test-media-center-no-kotlin.sh. Regenerating the template on a tauri-cli bump is the one legitimate reason to update a hash.

generated_kotlin._doc: Written at BUILD time into android_project/app/src/main/java/<identifier>/generated/ by tauri's and wry's build scripts (TAURI_ANDROID_PROJECT_PATH / WRY_ANDROID_KOTLIN_FILES_OUT_DIR, set by the tauri CLI), gitignored by the template. The guard accepts exactly these names there and only while git does not track them, and build.sh re-runs it after gradle so a build that grew a file the pin does not name fails.

tauri._doc_build_scripts: The only *.gradle.kts files allowed: the template's three, plus app/tauri.build.gradle.kts, which tauri-build writes at build time (gitignored by the template).

android._doc_application_id: A NEW identity, not the old media-center one: com.diegonmarcos.mediacenter belongs to cloud-gallery and is installed on phones, so this app takes com.diegonmarcos.cloudmediacenter, the package ac_cloud-me/build.json::ui.external_apps[cloud-media-center] already names for Cloud Me's Media tiles.
android._doc_target_sdk: No storage permission and no runtime grant: the app reads only its own bundled pages. compile_sdk is what the Tauri Android library compiles against.
android._doc_gradle_module: The Tauri project's app module; aa_cloud-superapp/test/test-app-names-pattern.sh T6 reads it to check the launcher label is build.json::name.

modules._doc: Shared modules the Tauri gradle project (tauri.android_project) includes BY REFERENCE beside the template's :app. Its settings.gradle iterates this map and, like every other reader of it (the ship workflow's trigger derivation, the publish gate, ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/shared-modules.test.sh), resolves each dir against THIS directory, not against the gradle root three levels down. They are compiled Kotlin libraries, not source in this app's tree, so test/test-media-center-no-kotlin.sh does not see them. libs:devtools finds this file by walking up from the gradle root (src-tauri/gen/android), as libs:analytics does, so there is one declaration and no copy.

libs:core._doc_dir: Fleet mesh membership: core manifest-merges the CONSTELLATION_DATA signature permission (defined and requested). Declared so a core change rebuilds this app instead of shipping a stale mesh member.

libs:devtools._doc_dir: Pulled in by core's `api project(':libs:devtools')` (FleetTokenProvider, FleetMemberReceiver, MESH_MEMBER <queries>); not linked directly. Listed so its changes also trigger a rebuild, and because Gradle resolves core's project path against this app's settings.gradle.

libs:crash._doc: #1122 libs:core `api`s this module (the default crash handler, the local crash sink and the generic crash screen); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:fleetconfig-model._doc: #873 libs:core `api`s this module (the setup provider every app serves, describe / export / apply / status); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:ui-nav-bars._doc: #1352 Configs ▸ General and ▸ About (fleetconfigs): FleetConfigsActivity, started from this app's own menu. Shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:bottomnav._doc: libs:ui-nav-bars' `api` dependency; listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

libs:ui-icons._doc: libs:bottomnav's dependency; listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

libs:theme-background._doc: libs:ui-nav-bars' `api` dependency (the page background); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

libs:perms._doc: #1360/#1352 libs:ui-nav-bars' `api` dependency: Configs ▸ General ▸ Perms is libs:perms' AppPermsSection, first run asks every never-asked grant.

toolchain._doc: Pinned here, read by the ship workflow and mirrored in flake.nix. agp/gradle/kotlin are the versions the pinned tauri-cli's Android template generates (src-tauri/gen/android/build.gradle.kts, gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties); gradle itself comes from the committed wrapper.

tauri_cli._doc: The prebuilt CLI tauri publishes for cargo-binstall (tauri-cli Cargo.toml [package.metadata.binstall]); the workflow downloads exactly this file and refuses any other sha256. The x86_64 build is the only Linux one published, so the APK is built on ubuntu-latest for every ABI (NDK cross-compile).

toolchain._doc_rust: Stable channel, no nightly feature; tauri 2.12 needs rustc >= 1.90. The ship workflow installs it through dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable with the Android targets tauri.targets names.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps, resolved by build.sh::_resolve_signing from the vault. No fallback key.

release._doc: Per-APK distribution, same data-driven block as every app here; build.sh oras-push and gh-release read it.

variants._doc: supported_abis is exactly the one ABI each APK's Rust library is built for.

release._doc_names: cloud-media-center.apk, cloud-media-center-x86_64.apk and the cloud-media-center GHCR image were the gallery's until its 2026-10 rename to cloud-gallery; they now carry this app. The gallery's own fleet entries moved to the cloud-gallery names in the same change, and Android treats this APK's different package as a different app, so installing it never replaces the gallery.

tests._doc: Read by 1_cicd/dist/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh, which the ship workflow runs before it builds.

shell._doc_requires: node runs the pages' pure render functions against the committed data to prove each page draws what web/data says. A tester that shells out to a tool which is not installed does not fail, it answers from the tool's absence, so a missing one is fatal at the engine's preflight.

data._doc: Where web/data/*.json comes from: data/regen.py fetches these paths from source.repo at source.commit (raw.githubusercontent.com, pinned, never a branch) and writes the compact page data the web/ pages read. Re-run it to move the pin; the pages never fetch at runtime.

shared._doc: The legal multi-source player's declarations, shared with My Movies (diegonmarcos.github.io c_Circus/movies) and pinned separately from data.source: regen.py fetches these at THIS commit and writes them verbatim (sources -> web/data/sources.json, denylist -> test/legal-denylist.json, core -> web/assets/sources-core.js wrapped as a plain script). Change the list in that repo, then move this pin and re-run regen.

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json, #1352 v2). general.sections: the anchors of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs; update is added after perms by default). about: the hand-written part of the extensive About: tagline, description, features, screens, guide, privacy, backends (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time), related fleet apps, credits for a fork. Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

about.tagline: Music, video, books and films in one hub
about.description: Cloud Media Center is the fleet's media hub, in Rust and static web only (a Tauri 2 app): seven mobile-first pages — music, videos, gallery, books, feed, movies and documentaries — built from the media data of the owner's public site pinned at one commit. Every link out opens the phone's own apps. It exists to make the owner's curated media collection browsable offline on the phone.
features: Works offline: the data ships with the app
guide: Open a page from the bottom bar.
Tap an item to open it in the phone's player or browser.
Update the app from Cloud Store to get the newest collection.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. It calls no fleet service: its data stays on the phone.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
